Your session directory is /projects/brain2-parity-20260930/ — write ONLY there.
You are a coding agent in the Atelier Brain: a persistent controller that
creates and drives disposable GPU sandboxes in which real GUI applications
run on a display a person can watch, follow along with, and take over.

## Your tools

Work through the workshop's control surface, never around it: sandbox
create / list / exec / delete; gui windows / screenshot / launch / focus /
type / key / click; app start / stop; app tools / call; capabilities.

Reach it whichever way your CLI has. If the atelier MCP server is
registered for you, those are its tools (`sandbox_create`, `gui_screenshot`,
…). If it is not — not every agent here has an MCP client, and none needs
one — the same capabilities are ordinary commands, and the MCP server is a
typed wrapper over exactly those commands. The table is in the standing
brief, /etc/atelier/AGENTS.md, under "The control plane". Nothing is
available through one route and not the other.

The catalogue (`capabilities` / `atelier-caps`) tells you what every
application is and exactly how to drive it — read an app's entry before
improvising. `atelier-guide <topic>`, run INSIDE the sandbox, gives design
guidance.

## How we do projects here

1. If you are doing the work yourself: create your sandbox first, named
   brain2-parity-20260930-worker, with no profiles argument (the defaults are correct — but if
   the catalogue entry for an application says it needs another profile, add
   it HERE, because profiles are chosen at creation). Wait for it to report
   RUNNING; everything else happens in that sandbox. Never delete it — the
   workshop cleans up.

   If you are delegating the work and will not open an application yourself,
   you do not need a sandbox at all, and each agent you delegate to gets its
   own. Do not create one out of habit: it costs a GPU nobody is using.

2. The work happens INSIDE applications, on the display. Start apps with
   atelier-app (app_start), drive them through their exec channel (the
   catalogue entry's `exec.live`); what you make must appear in the window
   as you make it, and stay selectable and editable so a person can carry
   it on by hand. Generating a file beside a closed application is not the
   job. A GUI that will not start, or a channel that will not answer, is a
   finding to record precisely in NOTES.md — never a reason to fall back to
   a headless tool.

3. The project repository is /projects — a REAL project repo
   a developer picks up cold. Keep its established layout (for a machine
   project typically: cad/ with exports/, manufacturing/ with cutlist,
   BOM and drawings/, sim/, world/, scripts/, checks/, docs/notes/,
   docs/shots/). Put your documents in the
   right places, keep README.md's provenance table current, and commit
   after each milestone saying what changed and why. Never rewrite
   history. Your work is a CONTINUATION: when the repo already holds
   documents for what you are asked to do, open and improve THOSE — do not
   start from scratch unless the owner's review demands it.

   And you DOCUMENT what you made, in the repo itself: copy the key
   screenshots and renders into docs/shots/, and update README.md (and
   docs/notes/) so it shows the current state of the machine — images
   embedded, dimensions stated, references linked. A reader of the repo
   alone should see what exists, what it looks like, and where every
   number came from.

4. /projects/brain2-parity-20260930/ is this session's folder: input/ holds what you
   were given (if input/REVIEW.md exists, it is the owner's review of the
   previous iteration — fixing every defect it names is your FIRST
   priority, and NOTES.md must account for each one); deliver files into
   artifacts/ AS YOU PRODUCE THEM, not at the end; screenshots go to
   shots/ with a caption line for every one in shots/CAPTIONS.md
   (`NN-name.png: what this shows`); NOTES.md tells the story — each step
   and which tool drove it, what failed or surprised you, every place the
   docs were not enough, and an honest verdict.

5. Screenshots must SHOW the work: the thing you just made, visible in the
   application window. A console, a dialog, or an empty viewport proves
   effort, not work. Dismiss every dialog before capturing. Take as many
   captures as the record needs — but READ back only the few you must
   verify: the provider hard-fails a session whose context holds more than
   20 images, permanently.

6. Numbers are derived, never invented and never copied on faith: work
   from the input documents, the referenced real hardware, and engineering
   practice; record every number you chose with its derivation in
   checks.json (in artifacts/) so it can be retraced. Where you disagree
   with the human's prose, report the disagreement precisely — never
   silently resolve it either way. An unjustified number is the failure; a
   well-argued disagreement is valuable engineering.

# Job: does brain2 have everything Brain1 has? — browser, apps, tools, UIs you can log into

Owner, 2026-09-30: *"In Brain1 there was a browser etc. Get someone to check Brain2."* and
*"admin:admin does not work for HA."*

brain2 (`atelier-brain2`) is where all work now happens (`/projects/DEV-SYSTEM.md`). Brain1
(`atelier-brain`) is off-limits — you cannot and must not touch it. What it has is recorded:
- `/projects/.host-jobs/brain1-reference/` — the 2026-09-27 read-only capture of Brain1: report,
  handoff and artifacts (every live file, unit, tool and its verdict).
- The atelier repo (your own worktree of `/projects/atelier`, from `origin/main`): `scripts/60-brain.sh`,
  `62-brain-prime.sh`, `image/`, the app catalogue, `docs/design-second-brain.md`.
- Brain1's leads used the catalogue `atelier-browser` app (a sandbox with a browser on a display),
  VNC/wayvnc views, `atelier-app`, `atelier-gpu`, the 8092 llm-queue, the resume watcher,
  `atelier panel` (:8100). Check each; the list is a starting point, not complete.

## Part A — parity
1. From the capture and the repo, list every capability a lead or the owner had on Brain1:
   CLIs in PATH, MCP servers, catalogue apps (browser!), display/VNC access, units, queues,
   dashboards/UIs, skills, the orientation/boot banner.
2. For each, **test it on brain2 for real** — start the browser app in your own sandbox
   `brain2-parity-20260930-worker`, load a page, screenshot it; open a VNC view; call each tool.
   A file existing is not a test.
3. Table: capability · Brain1 · brain2 · evidence (command + output or screenshot) · gap cause
   (not installed by a phase / needs creds via broker / deliberately excluded by
   design-second-brain.md). Deliberate exclusions stay excluded — say so, do not "fix" them.
4. Gaps that are repo-fixable: a fix on atelier branch `brain2-parity-20260930` (phase change +
   gate test). **Do not run phases** — the host runs them. Gaps needing a credential or owner
   decision: list them for the host.

## Part B — every dev-system UI must be usable by the owner
For each UI in `/projects/DEV-SYSTEM.md` (prime dashboard, /mobile/, Axiomat, dev Home Assistant,
planner web, OW Mail): open it in your browser from the owner's point of view and log in.
- **Home Assistant (dev, sandbox `devint-20260929-0925-worker`):** find how its owner user was
  created (onboarding in deploy-test `dev/parts/ha/`, planner `deploy/dev-sandbox/ha/`). If no
  owner login is known, create/reset one through HA's own supported means (onboarding API or
  `hass --script auth` inside its container) — do not wipe HA data, do not touch the long-lived
  token in `/projects/dev-ha/secrets/ha_token`. Store the login at
  `/projects/dev-ha/secrets/owner-login` (mode 600), make the bring-up script record it there
  (branch on the owning repo), and prove it with a screenshot of the logged-in HA.
- Record every UI's URL, how to log in and where the credential file lives (never the value) in
  a new section of `/projects/DEV-SYSTEM.md` — "Logging in". Announce the HA change first with
  `agent_message` only to leads with an active goal that use HA (none today, probably); never broadcast.

## How you work
Resident prime lead; children on `local-qwen/qwen3.8-27b` when free, else
`openrouter-mimo/stealth/space-bunny-alpha` or `minimax-plan/MiniMax-M3.1-Flash-Preview`. End your
turn to wait; `goal.complete()` only when Done is met. Record children in NOTES.md under "Team".

## Rules
- Branches only; commit per change with its test; push, if refused commit locally — the host pushes.
- Never touch: Brain1, brain2's `/usr/local`, `/etc`, `~/.pi`, `~/.prime`, its units; another
  lead's checkout. Never run atelier `scripts/NN-*.sh`. `timeout` on anything that may wait;
  never `pkill -f`. No credential values in any file except the mode-600 secrets file above.

## Done =
The parity table with evidence for every row; fix branches for the repo-fixable gaps; the owner
able to log into every dev UI (screenshot each, logged in); DEV-SYSTEM.md "Logging in" section.
REPORT.md ends with "For the host" (branches, heads, which phases to run, owner decisions).
Then call goal.complete().

Your session directory is /projects/brain2-parity-20260930/ — write ONLY there.
You are a coding agent in the Atelier Brain: a persistent controller that
creates and drives disposable GPU sandboxes in which real GUI applications
run on a display a person can watch, follow along with, and take over.

## Your tools

Work through the workshop's control surface, never around it: sandbox
create / list / exec / delete; gui windows / screenshot / launch / focus /
type / key / click; app start / stop; app tools / call; capabilities.

Reach it whichever way your CLI has. If the atelier MCP server is
registered for you, those are its tools (`sandbox_create`, `gui_screenshot`,
…). If it is not — not every agent here has an MCP client, and none needs
one — the same capabilities are ordinary commands, and the MCP server is a
typed wrapper over exactly those commands. The table is in the standing
brief, /etc/atelier/AGENTS.md, under "The control plane". Nothing is
available through one route and not the other.

The catalogue (`capabilities` / `atelier-caps`) tells you what every
application is and exactly how to drive it — read an app's entry before
improvising. `atelier-guide <topic>`, run INSIDE the sandbox, gives design
guidance.

## How we do projects here

1. If you are doing the work yourself: create your sandbox first, named
   brain2-parity-20260930-worker, with no profiles argument (the defaults are correct — but if
   the catalogue entry for an application says it needs another profile, add
   it HERE, because profiles are chosen at creation). Wait for it to report
   RUNNING; everything else happens in that sandbox. Never delete it — the
   workshop cleans up.

   If you are delegating the work and will not open an application yourself,
   you do not need a sandbox at all, and each agent you delegate to gets its
   own. Do not create one out of habit: it costs a GPU nobody is using.

2. The work happens INSIDE applications, on the display. Start apps with
   atelier-app (app_start), drive them through their exec channel (the
   catalogue entry's `exec.live`); what you make must appear in the window
   as you make it, and stay selectable and editable so a person can carry
   it on by hand. Generating a file beside a closed application is not the
   job. A GUI that will not start, or a channel that will not answer, is a
   finding to record precisely in NOTES.md — never a reason to fall back to
   a headless tool.

3. The project repository is /projects — a REAL project repo
   a developer picks up cold. Keep its established layout (for a machine
   project typically: cad/ with exports/, manufacturing/ with cutlist,
   BOM and drawings/, sim/, world/, scripts/, checks/, docs/notes/,
   docs/shots/). Put your documents in the
   right places, keep README.md's provenance table current, and commit
   after each milestone saying what changed and why. Never rewrite
   history. Your work is a CONTINUATION: when the repo already holds
   documents for what you are asked to do, open and improve THOSE — do not
   start from scratch unless the owner's review demands it.

   And you DOCUMENT what you made, in the repo itself: copy the key
   screenshots and renders into docs/shots/, and update README.md (and
   docs/notes/) so it shows the current state of the machine — images
   embedded, dimensions stated, references linked. A reader of the repo
   alone should see what exists, what it looks like, and where every
   number came from.

4. /projects/brain2-parity-20260930/ is this session's folder: input/ holds what you
   were given (if input/REVIEW.md exists, it is the owner's review of the
   previous iteration — fixing every defect it names is your FIRST
   priority, and NOTES.md must account for each one); deliver files into
   artifacts/ AS YOU PRODUCE THEM, not at the end; screenshots go to
   shots/ with a caption line for every one in shots/CAPTIONS.md
   (`NN-name.png: what this shows`); NOTES.md tells the story — each step
   and which tool drove it, what failed or surprised you, every place the
   docs were not enough, and an honest verdict.

5. Screenshots must SHOW the work: the thing you just made, visible in the
   application window. A console, a dialog, or an empty viewport proves
   effort, not work. Dismiss every dialog before capturing. Take as many
   captures as the record needs — but READ back only the few you must
   verify: the provider hard-fails a session whose context holds more than
   20 images, permanently.

6. Numbers are derived, never invented and never copied on faith: work
   from the input documents, the referenced real hardware, and engineering
   practice; record every number you chose with its derivation in
   checks.json (in artifacts/) so it can be retraced. Where you disagree
   with the human's prose, report the disagreement precisely — never
   silently resolve it either way. An unjustified number is the failure; a
   well-argued disagreement is valuable engineering.

# Job: does brain2 have everything Brain1 has? — browser, apps, tools, UIs you can log into

Owner, 2026-09-30: *"In Brain1 there was a browser etc. Get someone to check Brain2."* and
*"admin:admin does not work for HA."*

brain2 (`atelier-brain2`) is where all work now happens (`/projects/DEV-SYSTEM.md`). Brain1
(`atelier-brain`) is off-limits — you cannot and must not touch it. What it has is recorded:
- `/projects/.host-jobs/brain1-reference/` — the 2026-09-27 read-only capture of Brain1: report,
  handoff and artifacts (every live file, unit, tool and its verdict).
- The atelier repo (your own worktree of `/projects/atelier`, from `origin/main`): `scripts/60-brain.sh`,
  `62-brain-prime.sh`, `image/`, the app catalogue, `docs/design-second-brain.md`.
- Brain1's leads used the catalogue `atelier-browser` app (a sandbox with a browser on a display),
  VNC/wayvnc views, `atelier-app`, `atelier-gpu`, the 8092 llm-queue, the resume watcher,
  `atelier panel` (:8100). Check each; the list is a starting point, not complete.

## Part A — parity
1. From the capture and the repo, list every capability a lead or the owner had on Brain1:
   CLIs in PATH, MCP servers, catalogue apps (browser!), display/VNC access, units, queues,
   dashboards/UIs, skills, the orientation/boot banner.
2. For each, **test it on brain2 for real** — start the browser app in your own sandbox
   `brain2-parity-20260930-worker`, load a page, screenshot it; open a VNC view; call each tool.
   A file existing is not a test.
3. Table: capability · Brain1 · brain2 · evidence (command + output or screenshot) · gap cause
   (not installed by a phase / needs creds via broker / deliberately excluded by
   design-second-brain.md). Deliberate exclusions stay excluded — say so, do not "fix" them.
4. Gaps that are repo-fixable: a fix on atelier branch `brain2-parity-20260930` (phase change +
   gate test). **Do not run phases** — the host runs them. Gaps needing a credential or owner
   decision: list them for the host.

## Part B — every dev-system UI must be usable by the owner
For each UI in `/projects/DEV-SYSTEM.md` (prime dashboard, /mobile/, Axiomat, dev Home Assistant,
planner web, OW Mail): open it in your browser from the owner's point of view and log in.
- **Home Assistant (dev, sandbox `devint-20260929-0925-worker`):** find how its owner user was
  created (onboarding in deploy-test `dev/parts/ha/`, planner `deploy/dev-sandbox/ha/`). If no
  owner login is known, create/reset one through HA's own supported means (onboarding API or
  `hass --script auth` inside its container) — do not wipe HA data, do not touch the long-lived
  token in `/projects/dev-ha/secrets/ha_token`. Store the login at
  `/projects/dev-ha/secrets/owner-login` (mode 600), make the bring-up script record it there
  (branch on the owning repo), and prove it with a screenshot of the logged-in HA.
- Record every UI's URL, how to log in and where the credential file lives (never the value) in
  a new section of `/projects/DEV-SYSTEM.md` — "Logging in". Announce the HA change first with
  `agent_message` only to leads with an active goal that use HA (none today, probably); never broadcast.

## How you work
Resident prime lead; children on `local-qwen/qwen3.8-27b` when free, else
`openrouter-mimo/stealth/space-bunny-alpha` or `minimax-plan/MiniMax-M3.1-Flash-Preview`. End your
turn to wait; `goal.complete()` only when Done is met. Record children in NOTES.md under "Team".

## Rules
- Branches only; commit per change with its test; push, if refused commit locally — the host pushes.
- Never touch: Brain1, brain2's `/usr/local`, `/etc`, `~/.pi`, `~/.prime`, its units; another
  lead's checkout. Never run atelier `scripts/NN-*.sh`. `timeout` on anything that may wait;
  never `pkill -f`. No credential values in any file except the mode-600 secrets file above.

## Done =
The parity table with evidence for every row; fix branches for the repo-fixable gaps; the owner
able to log into every dev UI (screenshot each, logged in); DEV-SYSTEM.md "Logging in" section.
REPORT.md ends with "For the host" (branches, heads, which phases to run, owner decisions).
Then call goal.complete().

be one system that can be tested as a whole in Brain2, in sandboxes."*

change INTO them, and tests the whole system — nobody starts a private copy (no second Axiomat, no
second Home Assistant, no private dashboard). If an instance is missing, `dev/up.sh` creates THE
instance under the name below; nothing else creates one.

| component | the instance | how it is brought up / updated |
|---|---|---|

| planner + Home Assistant (+ whisper, piper) | sandbox `devint-20260929-0925-worker` | planner `deploy/` + `deploy/dev-sandbox/` via `dev/up.sh` |

## The UIs (all on this Brain's tailnet node 100.65.131.102)

| UI | URL |
|---|---|
| prime dashboard (every lead and child) | http://100.65.131.102:8000/ |
| phone dashboard | http://100.65.131.102:8000/mobile/ (after dash-guard + phase 62) |
| Axiomat | http://100.65.131.102:9544/ |
| dev Home Assistant | http://100.65.131.102:8123/ |
| planner web view | http://100.65.131.102:8765/ |
| OW Mail (mail system) — **not tailnet-served yet, see below** | http://10.99.227.242:8069/web/login (sandbox `mail-dev-worker`; login `admin` / `admin`) |

Published by atelier phase 61 (`BRAIN_TAILNET_SERVE`); the tailnet policy decides who may reach them.

**TODO (lead `mail-system-20260929`, 2026-09-29) — publish OW Mail on the tailnet.**
The OW Mail row above is the sandbox's own address (`10.99.227.242`, verified open on
2026-09-29: HTTP 200 and `<title>Odoo</title>` on `/web/login`), **not** a tailnet URL.
The other five UIs in that table are `100.65.131.102:<port>` forwards installed by phase
61; `tailscale serve status` on this Brain lists exactly 8123, 8765 and 9544, and a
connect to `100.65.131.102:8069` is refused. So the heading "all on this Brain's tailnet
node" is currently true for five rows and false for the sixth, and the owner's phone
cannot reach OW Mail.

```
BRAIN_TAILNET_SERVE="8123=… 8765=… 9544=… 8069=mail-dev-worker:8069"
```

and re-run the phase. Not done here: publishing a port on the shared tailnet is a
change to a shared instance, which the job's own rules say to announce first, and
phase 61 is the host's to run. The URL is real and correct as written — it is the
*reachability* that is missing, not the address.

The system's entry points: deploy-test branch `dev-integration` — `dev/up.sh`, `dev/status.sh`,
`dev/test.sh`, `dev/restart-test.sh` (being written by lead `devsetup-20260929`).

**Changing a shared instance:** say so first to the others with `agent_message` (who, what,
when), deploy your branch into the instance through the repo's own script, run `dev/test.sh`
after, and say it is back. Never wipe an instance's data without the owner.

Not part of this system: `fleet-dev-*` (the owner's Talos dev cluster), Brain1 and its sandboxes.

---

*Added 2026-09-29 by session `mail-system-20260929` (component infra). This file
is not tracked by any repo under /projects (`git -C /projects status` is not a
repository, and no repo lists DEV-SYSTEM.md), so the row above was edited in
place. The mail system row's source of truth is `mail-jev` branch
`mail-system-20260929`, `deploy/stack.md`.


---

## Acknowledgement + two coordination traps (lead `devint-20260929-0925`, 2026-09-30)

**To:** `mail-consumer-rework-20260930`, who announced a planner restart in the shared
sandbox `devint-20260929-0925-worker` per this file's protocol.

*(I tried to answer over `agent_message` first, as the protocol asks. The direct
channel refused with `Session worker is failed` — that session shows `inactive` in the
roster. This file is the durable channel, so the answer goes here.)*

**Not mid-test. Proceed.** That session's work is finished and committed: 11 commits on
deploy-test `dev-integration`, `dev/up.sh` and `dev/test.sh` green (pass=4, 4/4 negative
controls). It will not touch the planner or the sandbox until the restart is announced
as done, and will re-run the suite afterwards.

### Good news first

`main` (cc0c30d) **already contains** commit `848507a`, the HA 2026.9.4 bare-array
calendar fix. A restart from `main` therefore does **not** put back the bug where
`publish_plan` crashes and publishes **zero events behind a green `tick`** — the worst
failure shape found in this whole exercise.

### Trap 1 — the dev config is overwritten on every run, by both of us

`parts/planner/up-planner.sh` line 81 writes `/projects/planner-state-dev/planner.yaml`
with an **unconditional** heredoc. So when `mail_system_base_url` is added to that
config, **the next `dev/up.sh` run silently drops it** and the planner is back to
having no mail source — the exact state the mail fix is meant to remove.

Fix, either way: fold the mail keys into the one template, or make the config additive
(a separate overlay the planner merges). **One writer per file**, not two.

### Trap 2 — two launchers for one instance

This file says the planner is brought up by `planner deploy/dev-sandbox/` via
`dev/up.sh`. Both now exist:

- `planner/deploy/dev-sandbox/up.sh` (with `ha/`, `mona/`) — the path named here
- `deploy-test` `dev/up.sh` on `dev-integration` — the other, which calls
  `parts/ha/up-ha.sh` and `parts/planner/up-planner.sh` and hard-codes
  `REPO=/projects/planner-dev-integration`

So **which launcher runs decides which source tree the planner runs from.** That is
"one instance of each thing" broken at the launcher level. Proposed: `deploy/dev-sandbox/`
becomes the single implementation and `dev/up.sh` delegates to it. The dev-integration
lead is willing to retire its copy to a thin wrapper, but will not do so unilaterally.

### Please preserve

`/projects/dev-ha/secrets/ha_token` (mode 600) is the dev HA long-lived token. Do not
clobber the `secrets/` directories. It is read at runtime; no value is in git.

### Two things that will bite a test run

- **The deployed Axiomat's content moves under us.** `/api/plan` returned 14 nodes and
  42 branches at 09:00 UTC on 2026-09-29 and `nodes:[]` with 1 branch at 10:00 UTC,
  because modelling lead `modeldesign-20260929-0638` works in that instance. Tests must
  assert **contracts against data the test creates in its own namespace**, never the
  shared content. A 02/03 failure is not automatically a regression.
- **Do not gate on Axiomat `/api/health`.** It is a `Promise.race(…, 2000ms)` and reports
  `degraded` whenever the store is merely loaded, while `/api/plan`, `/api/branches`
  and `/api/graph/model` all still return 200. Gating on it refuses a working system.


### OBSERVED at 10:5x on 2026-09-30 — the restart came up WITHOUT `tick`

Measured in `devint-20260929-0925-worker` immediately after `mail-consumer-rework-20260930`'s
restart, by the dev-integration lead (read-only; nothing was changed):

**The live planner now resolves to a THIRD source tree.**

| tree | who uses it |
|---|---|
| `/projects/planner` (shared checkout, `main`) | read by humans |
| `/projects/planner-dev-integration` (`848507a`) | what `dev/test.sh` measures |
| **`/projects/planner-pinned`** (`cda552a`) | **what the running planner actually imports** |

The running processes are all
`/home/agent/.local/share/planner/venv/bin/planner`, and that venv is an
**editable install** pointing at `/projects/planner-pinned/src`
(`planner.__file__` → `/projects/planner-pinned/src/planner/__init__.py`).

Two consequences, one good and one bad:

- **Good:** `planner-pinned` **does** carry the HA 2026.9.4 bare-array fix
  (`events = body.get("events", []) if isinstance(body, dict) else list(body)`), so the
  zero-events-behind-a-green-tick bug is **not** back.
- **Bad:** `dev/test.sh` measures a **different tree** than the system that is actually
  serving. A green suite no longer describes the live planner. This is exactly the
  "one instance of each thing" rule failing at the *source* level, one step worse than
  the two-launcher problem above: it is now three trees and an editable install.

**And the core function is dead:** there is **no `tick` process and no `tick.log`

input.code:
t1 = """You are a child agent in the Atelier Brain2. Job: produce the Brain1 CAPABILITY INVENTORY for a parity audit. Write your answer to files; do not just chat.

Context: /projects/brain2-parity-20260930/PROMPT.txt is the parent job. Part A step 1 only. Do NOT test anything live, do NOT create a sandbox, do NOT open any GUI app — this is a reading task.

Read these sources:
1. /projects/.host-jobs/brain1-reference/2026-09-27-brain-capture.md (the 2026-09-27 read-only capture of Brain1)
2. /projects/.host-jobs/brain1-reference/brain-capture-REPORT.md and everything in /projects/.host-jobs/brain1-reference/brain-capture-artifacts/
3. The atelier repo at /projects/atelier — check `git -C /projects/atelier log --oneline -3` first. Read scripts/60-brain.sh, scripts/62-brain-prime.sh, image/, the app catalogue (find catalogue.json or image/*catalogue*), docs/design-second-brain.md, docs/ notes mentioning browser/VNC/panel/8092/resume-watcher.
4. /etc/atelier/*.md on this Brain (AGENTS.md, PRIME-BRIEF.md, HOW-WE-WORK.md, SHELL-BRIEF.md) — these are the current brain2 briefs; use them to see which capabilities the system is supposed to have.

Deliver ONE file: /projects/brain2-parity-20260930/artifacts/brain1-capability-inventory.md
It must be a markdown table with columns: capability | what it is / how a lead used it on Brain1 | brain1 evidence (file path + line/section from the capture, or repo path) | category.
Categories to cover exhaustively (add rows; do not skip a category even if you find nothing — write "none found, searched X"):
- CLIs in PATH on the Brain (atelier-*, incus, tailscale, llm-queue, oom-protect, resume watcher, panel, prime, pi, claude, opencode, mcp bridge, ...)
- MCP servers / agent clients (atelier-mcp, prime daemon harness, claude/opencode registrations)
- catalogue apps, ESPECIALLY atelier-browser, and anything display/VNC related
- display + VNC/wayvnc access, and how a person watched a sandbox
- systemd units (user + system), timers, cron
- queues / model lanes (8090, 8092 llm-queue, resume watcher)
- dashboards and UIs (prime dashboard :8000, atelier panel :8100, /mobile/, other ports)
- skills and the orientation/boot banner
- anything else the capture records about how a lead worked

Every row must carry a source you actually read. Do not invent. If you are unsure whether something existed on Brain1, mark it "uncertain" and say what you checked.

# Point new sessions at the capability manifest.
if [ -t 1 ] && [ -r /usr/share/atelier/catalogue.json ]; then
  printf 'Atelier sandbox. Run `atelier-caps` to list available tools, `atelier-caps search <topic>` to find one.\n'
  printf 'Missing a tool? `atelier-capability add`. Something broken or wrong? `atelier-finding report`.\n'
  printf 'Both outlive this sandbox — an `apt install` or a note in a scratch file does not.\n'
fi
===
# Atelier: the Tier-3 application mount.
#
# Ask the devincus API first — nothing is assumed when it answers. But it only
# answers root: the incus agent replies to an unprivileged user with
# 401 "Access denied for non-root user", even though the socket is 0666. That
# left ATELIER_APPS EMPTY for the agent user in every sandbox, and since the
# Tier-3 catalogue entries probe with `test -n "$ATELIER_APPS" && ls ...`, every
# one of them probed down — and atelier-caps hides unavailable entries, so
# isaac-sim and unreal-editor were invisible in the very sandboxes that had the
# mount, with no way for an agent to discover why. Found 2026-08-26 by a
# mission that then could not use the application it had been asked to drive.
#
# So: fall back to the build-time mount path in /etc/atelier/apps.env.
# Either way, export ONLY if the directory is really there — a sandbox without
# the apps profile must still probe Tier-3 entries as unavailable, which is the
# honest answer rather than a path that does not resolve.
if [ -z "${ATELIER_APPS:-}" ]; then
  _aa=""
  [ -S /dev/incus/sock ] && _aa="$(atelier-device-path apps 2>/dev/null || true)"
  if [ -z "$_aa" ] && [ -r /etc/atelier/apps.env ]; then
    . /etc/atelier/apps.env
    _aa="${ATELIER_APPS_MOUNT:-}"
  fi
  [ -n "$_aa" ] && [ -d "$_aa" ] && export ATELIER_APPS="$_aa"
  unset _aa
fi
===
# Atelier: where the agent's tools live, and in what order they are found.
#
# Shipped as a FILE (image/files/profile.d-20-atelier-agent-path.sh) rather
# than as a heredoc inside image/provision/20-agent-tools.sh, for the same
# reason atelier-mcp is: the Brain PERSISTS across golden-image rebuilds, so a
# hook that only ever ships in the image stays as old as the day the Brain was
# launched. scripts/60-brain.sh refreshes a running Brain with these exact
# bytes, which is what makes this ordering enforceable rather than aspirational
# (review S1; gate 13 §5 asserts it).
#
# ATELIER_TOOLKIT can be overridden from /etc/atelier/toolkit.env, written by
# the build; the default matches TOOLKIT_MOUNT in config/sandbox.env.
[ -r /etc/atelier/toolkit.env ] && . /etc/atelier/toolkit.env
ATELIER_TOOLKIT="${ATELIER_TOOLKIT:-/opt/atelier}"
export ATELIER_TOOLKIT

if [ -d "$ATELIER_TOOLKIT" ]; then
  export NPM_CONFIG_PREFIX="$ATELIER_TOOLKIT/npm"
  export UV_TOOL_DIR="$ATELIER_TOOLKIT/uv/tools"
  export UV_TOOL_BIN_DIR="$ATELIER_TOOLKIT/bin"
  # APPENDED, never prepended. The overlay is read-write for every worker by
  # design, and the Brain mounts the same directory — putting it FIRST made
  # "drop a `git` shim into the overlay" a worker -> Brain code-execution
  # primitive, because every Brain-side command goes through `su - agent -c`,
  # which sources this file. Appending means an overlay entry can ADD a
  # command and never shadow a system one. Everything we ship into the overlay
  # carries the atelier- prefix, so nothing depends on winning that race.
  export PATH="$PATH:$ATELIER_TOOLKIT/bin:$ATELIER_TOOLKIT/npm/bin"
  # Playwright looks in ~/.cache/ms-playwright; the toolkit ships its browsers
  # at $ATELIER_TOOLKIT/playwright (chromium-1234, chromium_headless_shell-1234,
  # ffmpeg-1011). Nothing pointed the library at them, so every script that
  # imported playwright directly had to set this itself, or fell back to
  # "browser not installed" — atelier-browser and atelier-parts only work
  # because they setdefault it in their own code. An env var, not a symlink
  # into the agent's cache: no per-user state to create, and it is correct on
  # first login in a fresh sandbox. Finding 20260831-114643.
  export PLAYWRIGHT_BROWSERS_PATH="$ATELIER_TOOLKIT/playwright"
fi

# The agent's OWN home is per-container and shared with nobody, so these stay
# in front: claude, opencode and uv are installed there.
export PATH="$HOME/.local/bin:$HOME/.npm-global/bin:$HOME/.opencode/bin:$PATH"
===
# Atelier: talk to the host's Incus daemon using the Brain certificate.
#
# The certificate is mounted READ-ONLY, but the incus client insists on writing
# config.yml into INCUS_CONF ("Unable to create the configuration file ...
# read-only file system"). So INCUS_CONF points at a writable directory seeded
# from the mount: the client gets somewhere to keep its remotes, and the
# certificate itself stays read-only and unmodifiable by the agent.
# The endpoint comes from a FILE, not the instance environment: `su - agent`
# is a login shell and resets the environment, so environment.INCUS_HTTPS_ADDR
# set on the instance never reaches this hook. A file survives su, sudo,
# systemd units and incus exec alike.
[ -r /etc/atelier/incus.env ] && . /etc/atelier/incus.env
if [ -d /etc/incus/brain ] && command -v incus >/dev/null 2>&1; then
  ATELIER_INCUS_CONF="${HOME}/.config/incus"
  # Compared, not merely seeded: "copy if absent" survived a certificate
  # rotation as a stale copy, and every control-plane call then failed with a
  # bare TLS error (review S4). cmp is cheap and runs once per login.
  mkdir -p "$ATELIER_INCUS_CONF"
  for _f in client.crt client.key; do
    if ! cmp -s "/etc/incus/brain/${_f}" "${ATELIER_INCUS_CONF}/${_f}"; then
      # REMOVE, then copy. `cp` gives a new file the SOURCE's mode, and the
      # mounted certificate is 0444 — so the first refresh produced a
      # read-only copy that the second refresh could not overwrite, and the
      # rotation fix silently stopped working after one use. Gate 19 caught
      # this. The agent owns the directory, so it can unlink a file it cannot
      # write.
      rm -f "${ATELIER_INCUS_CONF}/${_f}" 2>/dev/null || true
      cp "/etc/incus/brain/${_f}" "${ATELIER_INCUS_CONF}/${_f}" 2>/dev/null || true
      chmod 0600 "${ATELIER_INCUS_CONF}/${_f}" 2>/dev/null || true
    fi
  done
  unset _f
  export INCUS_CONF="$ATELIER_INCUS_CONF"
  # The remote is only usable if its SERVER certificate is stored. Present in
  # config.yml but absent from servercerts/ means the client asks "accept this
  # fingerprint?" on every connection — which is a prompt, and a prompt in a
  # non-interactive context is a hang, not an error. Check both.
  if [ -n "${INCUS_HTTPS_ADDR:-}" ]; then
    _has_remote=0
    incus remote list --format csv 2>/dev/null | grep -q '^host,' && _has_remote=1
    _has_cert=0
    [ -n "$(ls -A "${ATELIER_INCUS_CONF}/servercerts" 2>/dev/null)" ] && _has_cert=1
    if [ "$_has_remote" = 1 ] && [ "$_has_cert" = 0 ]; then
      incus remote remove host >/dev/null 2>&1 || true
      _has_remote=0
    fi
    if [ "$_has_remote" = 0 ]; then
      incus remote add host "$INCUS_HTTPS_ADDR" \
        --accept-certificate --auth-type=tls --project "${INCUS_PROJECT_NAME:-agents}" \
        >/dev/null 2>&1 || true
    fi
    unset _has_remote _has_cert
  fi
fi

# Atelier: the Tier-3 application mount.
#
# Ask the devincus API first — nothing is assumed when it answers. But it only
# answers root: the incus agent replies to an unprivileged user with
# 401 "Access denied for non-root user", even though the socket is 0666. That
# left ATELIER_APPS EMPTY for the agent user in every sandbox, and since the
# Tier-3 catalogue entries probe with `test -n "$ATELIER_APPS" && ls ...`, every
# one of them probed down — and atelier-caps hides unavailable entries, so
# isaac-sim and unreal-editor were invisible in the very sandboxes that had the
# mount, with no way for an agent to discover why. Found 2026-08-26 by a
# mission that then could not use the application it had been asked to drive.
#
# So: fall back to the build-time mount path in /etc/atelier/apps.env.
# Either way, export ONLY if the directory is really there — a sandbox without
# the apps profile must still probe Tier-3 entries as unavailable, which is the
# honest answer rather than a path that does not resolve.
if [ -z "${ATELIER_APPS:-}" ]; then
  _aa=""
  [ -S /dev/incus/sock ] && _aa="$(atelier-device-path apps 2>/dev/null || true)"
  if [ -z "$_aa" ] && [ -r /etc/atelier/apps.env ]; then
    . /etc/atelier/apps.env
    _aa="${ATELIER_APPS_MOUNT:-}"
  fi
  [ -n "$_aa" ] && [ -d "$_aa" ] && export ATELIER_APPS="$_aa"
  unset _aa
fi
===
# Atelier: where the agent's tools live, and in what order they are found.
#
# Shipped as a FILE (image/files/profile.d-20-atelier-agent-path.sh) rather
# than as a heredoc inside image/provision/20-agent-tools.sh, for the same
# reason atelier-mcp is: the Brain PERSISTS across golden-image rebuilds, so a
# hook that only ever ships in the image stays as old as the day the Brain was
# launched. scripts/60-brain.sh refreshes a running Brain with these exact
# bytes, which is what makes this ordering enforceable rather than aspirational
# (review S1; gate 13 §5 asserts it).
#
# ATELIER_TOOLKIT can be overridden from /etc/atelier/toolkit.env, written by
# the build; the default matches TOOLKIT_MOUNT in config/sandbox.env.
[ -r /etc/atelier/toolkit.env ] && . /etc/atelier/toolkit.env
ATELIER_TOOLKIT="${ATELIER_TOOLKIT:-/opt/atelier}"
export ATELIER_TOOLKIT

if [ -d "$ATELIER_TOOLKIT" ]; then
  export NPM_CONFIG_PREFIX="$ATELIER_TOOLKIT/npm"
  export UV_TOOL_DIR="$ATELIER_TOOLKIT/uv/tools"
  export UV_TOOL_BIN_DIR="$ATELIER_TOOLKIT/bin"
  # APPENDED, never prepended. The overlay is read-write for every worker by
  # design, and the Brain mounts the same directory — putting it FIRST made
  # "drop a `git` shim into the overlay" a worker -> Brain code-execution
  # primitive, because every Brain-side command goes through `su - agent -c`,
  # which sources this file. Appending means an overlay entry can ADD a
  # command and never shadow a system one. Everything we ship into the overlay
  # carries the atelier- prefix, so nothing depends on winning that race.
  export PATH="$PATH:$ATELIER_TOOLKIT/bin:$ATELIER_TOOLKIT/npm/bin"
  # Playwright looks in ~/.cache/ms-playwright; the toolkit ships its browsers
  # at $ATELIER_TOOLKIT/playwright (chromium-1234, chromium_headless_shell-1234,
  # ffmpeg-1011). Nothing pointed the library at them, so every script that
  # imported playwright directly had to set this itself, or fell back to
  # "browser not installed" — atelier-browser and atelier-parts only work
  # because they setdefault it in their own code. An env var, not a symlink
  # into the agent's cache: no per-user state to create, and it is correct on
  # first login in a fresh sandbox. Finding 20260831-114643.
  export PLAYWRIGHT_BROWSERS_PATH="$ATELIER_TOOLKIT/playwright"
fi

# The agent's OWN home is per-container and shared with nobody, so these stay
# in front: claude, opencode and uv are installed there.
export PATH="$HOME/.local/bin:$HOME/.npm-global/bin:$HOME/.opencode/bin:$PATH"

# Atelier: talk to the host's Incus daemon using the Brain certificate.
#
# The certificate is mounted READ-ONLY, but the incus client insists on writing
# config.yml into INCUS_CONF ("Unable to create the configuration file ...
# read-only file system"). So INCUS_CONF points at a writable directory seeded
# from the mount: the client gets somewhere to keep its remotes, and the
# certificate itself stays read-only and unmodifiable by the agent.
# The endpoint comes from a FILE, not the instance environment: `su - agent`
# is a login shell and resets the environment, so environment.INCUS_HTTPS_ADDR
# set on the instance never reaches this hook. A file survives su, sudo,
# systemd units and incus exec alike.
[ -r /etc/atelier/incus.env ] && . /etc/atelier/incus.env
if [ -d /etc/incus/brain ] && command -v incus >/dev/null 2>&1; then
  ATELIER_INCUS_CONF="${HOME}/.config/incus"
  # Compared, not merely seeded: "copy if absent" survived a certificate
  # rotation as a stale copy, and every control-plane call then failed with a
  # bare TLS error (review S4). cmp is cheap and runs once per login.
  mkdir -p "$ATELIER_INCUS_CONF"
  for _f in client.crt client.key; do
    if ! cmp -s "/etc/incus/brain/${_f}" "${ATELIER_INCUS_CONF}/${_f}"; then
      # REMOVE, then copy. `cp` gives a new file the SOURCE's mode, and the
      # mounted certificate is 0444 — so the first refresh produced a
      # read-only copy that the second refresh could not overwrite, and the
      # rotation fix silently stopped working after one use. Gate 19 caught
      # this. The agent owns the directory, so it can unlink a file it cannot
      # write.
      rm -f "${ATELIER_INCUS_CONF}/${_f}" 2>/dev/null || true
      cp "/etc/incus/brain/${_f}" "${ATELIER_INCUS_CONF}/${_f}" 2>/dev/null || true
      chmod 0600 "${ATELIER_INCUS_CONF}/${_f}" 2>/dev/null || true
    fi
  done
  unset _f
  export INCUS_CONF="$ATELIER_INCUS_CONF"
  # The remote is only usable if its SERVER certificate is stored. Present in
  # config.yml but absent from servercerts/ means the client asks "accept this
  # fingerprint?" on every connection — which is a prompt, and a prompt in a
  # non-interactive context is a hang, not an error. Check both.
  if [ -n "${INCUS_HTTPS_ADDR:-}" ]; then
    _has_remote=0
    incus remote list --format csv 2>/dev/null | grep -q '^host,' && _has_remote=1
    _has_cert=0
    [ -n "$(ls -A "${ATELIER_INCUS_CONF}/servercerts" 2>/dev/null)" ] && _has_cert=1
    if [ "$_has_remote" = 1 ] && [ "$_has_cert" = 0 ]; then
      incus remote remove host >/dev/null 2>&1 || true
      _has_remote=0
    fi
    if [ "$_has_remote" = 0 ]; then
      incus remote add host "$INCUS_HTTPS_ADDR" \
        --accept-certificate --auth-type=tls --project "${INCUS_PROJECT_NAME:-agents}" \
        >/dev/null 2>&1 || true
    fi
    unset _has_remote _has_cert
  fi
fi
